Caravan Finance Australia: Everything You Need to Know in 2026

Planning your big lap or looking for a weekend escape? Here's exactly how caravan finance works in Australia, what you can borrow, and how to get the best deal.

Australia has one of the most vibrant caravan and camping cultures in the world. Whether you're planning a Grey Nomad adventure or just want a reliable weekender, a quality van is a significant purchase — and for most Australians, financing makes it accessible without draining savings.

What Can Be Financed?

  • On-road caravans (pop-tops, full-height, slide-outs)
  • Off-road and semi-off-road caravans
  • Camper trailers (hard floor and soft floor)
  • Fifth-wheelers
  • Motorhomes and campervans
  • Accessories and solar setups (in many cases, bundled into the loan)

Both new and used caravans can be financed, including private sales — though the process for private sales involves a few extra steps to verify ownership and ensure there's no encumbrance on the asset.

Types of Caravan Finance

Consumer Loan (Secured)

The most straightforward option. The caravan acts as security for the loan, typically resulting in competitive rates and terms of up to 7 years. You own the caravan outright from day one.

Secured Personal Loan

Similar to a secured consumer loan but may offer slightly more flexibility around what's included in the loan. Works well for caravans bundled with accessories.

Chattel Mortgage (Business Use)

If you run a business that uses the caravan for income-generating purposes — for example, if you work remotely and travel for work — a chattel mortgage may be appropriate. Speak to your accountant about the eligibility requirements.

How Much Can I Borrow?

Lenders typically finance between $5,000 and $150,000 for leisure assets, depending on the asset value, your credit profile, and your income. Loan terms of 1–7 years are standard, with some lenders offering up to 10 years for higher-value purchases.

A deposit isn't always required — many lenders will finance the full purchase price for qualified applicants. However, a deposit reduces your repayments and demonstrates commitment, which can strengthen your application.

New vs Used Caravans — Does it Affect Finance?

New caravans generally attract lower rates and longer terms. Used caravans — especially older models — may have lender restrictions based on age (commonly, loans must be repaid before the van reaches a certain age). Off-road models may also be assessed differently by some lenders.

What to Check Before You Buy

  • Run a PPSR (Personal Property Securities Register) check to confirm no money is owed on the asset
  • Inspect the van thoroughly — water damage and structural issues are common in older models
  • Check if the van is listed with the correct compliance plate and tare weight
  • Confirm the total weight is within your tow vehicle's towing capacity
  • Get a caravan club inspection or independent assessment for higher-value purchases

Private Sale? We've Got You Covered

Financing a caravan from a private seller is possible through most lenders on our panel. We'll help with the PPSR check, ownership verification, and settlement to make the process smooth.

Whether you're planning a weekend trip to the Hinterland or a year on the road, getting the finance right from the start means you can focus on the adventure — not the paperwork.
